issue_context.title: Home Assistant Lights Not Working (ISY994 Integration) v0.109.1 (Video Included)
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
I originally thought this was a Lovelace issue, but it also affects the dev tools service tool. Please see the YouTube video below for a quick synopsis.

Basically, and I've only tested this for the ISY994 integration, starting with v0.109.0 or thereabouts, light.turn_on is sending DOF (turn off) when the current state of the light is off:

```
[homeassistant.components.isy994] ISY Request: http://192.168.1.3:80/rest/nodes/50%2033%208B%201/cmd/DOF
```

Adjusting the brightness value restores that single light switch to normal working order until a restart of Home Assistant. I've tried clearing my states table in home-assistant_v2.db and tried deleting the core.[device_registry,entity_registry,resore_state] files and it does not resolve this issue.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: v0.109.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): v0.109.1
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): venv
- Integration causing this issue: ISY994
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/isy994/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

N/A

## Traceback/Error logs
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X8iywbepeiQ

## Additional information
comments: @awgneo Thanks for the video.  which firmware do you have on the isy?

@bdraco Sure thing :) I have v5.0.16C on my ISY994. I've had this firmware on there for a couple of months, however. The recent update to 0.109.0/1 of HASS seems to be the culprit, but I could be wrong.
@awgneo Can you try the code in the PR I linked to this?
@bdraco will do later today :) thanks for approaching this so quickly
Thanks again for this! Everything working perfectly again :D

review_comments: How is this fixing the issue that we would send the turn off command? Shouldn't the fix be that we just send _any_ brightness and not just send `val=None`  ?
Or can we call `self._node.on()` without passing a value ?
